correctness.rationale: The commuting condition gives a unique phase-weighted partial injection between equal-length permutation cycles, and nilpotency is equivalent to directed path components. Every step of the exponential formula follows by labeling path vertices and independent phases; all ranks and cutoff support follow from elementary path compositions. Exhaustive independent direct-map calculations verify each coefficient for all cycle types on up to six points and a nontrivial eight-point centralizer. Finite checks are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Classical full inverse-monoid path decomposition (Gomes–Howie 1987) and Lah counts (Laradji–Umar and Ganyushkin–Mazorchuk 2004) are known and credited, as is Konieczny’s 2013 centralizer membership classification. The assessed statement is the uniform rank- and nilpotency-index-refined enumerator inside each arbitrary permutation centralizer together with sharp exact rank support; inspected full published theorems do not state it. The closest 2020 source was only abstract-accessible and is an explicit significant residual risk, not ruled out by title/abstract. No claim of absolute novelty is made.
residual_risks: The complete text of Konieczny (2020), directly addressing finite centralizers, was inaccessible; it could contain an equivalent or dominating counting formula.

value.rationale: For each permutation of every finite degree, the theorem provides the full joint rank/nilpotency-index distribution and all attainable rank values under an algebraically natural nilpotency constraint. The filtration by powers of zero and centralizer dependence on cycle type are canonical semigroup invariants, including non-contiguous rank spectra. It is stronger than a finite isolated example or known unconditioned Lah number; the sharp bound and support are exact and constructively attained.
